newsitem.title: FRANCE: French Socialists bury row over wiretaps.
newsitem.headline: French Socialists bury row over wiretaps.

text.p: France's opposition Socialists rushed on Wednesday to bury a damaging quarrel over whether their late leader Francois Mitterrand had the right to order illegal telephone wiretaps when president.
Socialist Party leader Lionel Jospin said Mitterrand's former confidant, Michel Charasse, had apologised to him for his attack on Jospin's criticism of the wiretaps.
He said Charasse telephoned and wrote to him to voice regrets for his stinging attack, made in a weekend radio interview.
Jospin has tried to distance the Socialists from the seamy side of Mitterrand's rule, calling for "monarchical secrecy" on wiretaps to be lifted.

Charasse, a former budget minister, said in the interview that Mitterrand was entirely justified, in a period of terrorist attacks and blackmail threats, in tapping the telephones of journalists, lawyers, politicians and actors.
He accused Jospin using the controversy to win votes and said he should not "betray a sense of state" if he hoped to govern France after next year's general election.
Charasse explained in his letter he gave the interview from a telephone box, in uncomfortable conditions.

But the apologies did not settle the disagreement between the two men. Charasse repeated in his letter he opposed lifting official secrecy on wiretapping, while Jospin said it must apply only when legally authorised on grounds of national security.

The disclosure last week that Mitterrand, who died last year seven months after leaving office, personally oversaw the illegal wiretapping of dozens of politicians, journalists and lawyers has embarrassed his Socialist Party.

It also embarrassed the conservative government as most politicians, left and right, united to criticise Gaullist Prime Minister Alain Juppe for refusing to lift official secrecy surrounding the affair.

Juppe, yielding to pressure to lift secrecy, decided on Tuesday that copious files uncovered by the security services shoould be given to an investigating magistrate if experts determined the wiretaps had been carried out illegally.
